claim: Lmx1b-deficient 5-HT neurons fail to generate axonal projections to the forebrain and spinal cord.
source: We report that LIM homeodomain factor 1b (Lmx1b)-deficient 5-HT neurons fail to generate axonal projections to the forebrain and spinal cord.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Lmx1b is required at successive stages to control 5-HT axon primary outgrowth, selective routing, and terminal arborization.
source: Stage-specific targeting demonstrates that Lmx1b is required at successive stages to control 5-HT axon primary outgrowth, selective routing, and terminal arborization.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding based on stage-specific targeting experiments.

claim: A Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade is temporally required for 5-HT arborization.
source: We show a Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade is temporally required for 5-HT arborization and upregulation of the 5-HT axon arborization gene, Protocadherin-alphac2, during postnatal development of forebrain 5-HT axons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: The Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade controls upregulation of Protocadherin-alphac2 during postnatal development of forebrain 5-HT axons.
source: We show a Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade is temporally required for 5-HT arborization and upregulation of the 5-HT axon arborization gene, Protocadherin-alphac2, during postnatal development of forebrain 5-HT axons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: 5-HT modulates the excitability of nearly all neural circuitry in the brain and spinal cord.
source: 5-HT modulates the excitability of nearly all neural circuitry in the brain and spinal cord despite being produced in a relatively small population of neurons (Azevedo et al., 2009; Baker et al., 1991; Hornung, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 5-HT is produced in a relatively small population of neurons.
source: 5-HT modulates the excitability of nearly all neural circuitry in the brain and spinal cord despite being produced in a relatively small population of neurons (Azevedo et al., 2009; Baker et al., 1991; Hornung, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Expansive serotonergic neuromodulation is achieved through the formation of long-range highly diffuse ascending and descending projection pathways.
source: Expansive serotonergic neuromodulation is achieved through the formation of long-range highly diffuse ascending and descending projection pathways that deliver 5-HT throughout the brain and spinal cord for synaptic or non-synaptic interactions with an array of receptors (Hannon and Hoyer, 2008; Steinbusch, 1981).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 5-HT neurons initiate axon outgrowth concomitant with their birth and onset of 5-HT synthesis.
source: 5-HT neurons initiate axon outgrowth concomitant with their birth and onset of 5-HT synthesis (Hawthorne et al., 2010; Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Formation of 5-HT projection pathways occurs in three successive stages: primary pathway formation, selective pathway routing, and postnatal terminal arborization.
source: Classic neuroanatomical studies have defined three successive stages, collectively spanning several weeks, in the formation of 5-HT projection pathways: primary pathway formation during which 5-HT axon outgrowth is initiated, selective pathway routing, and finally postnatal terminal arborization (Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Ascending 5-HT axons reach all forebrain targets at parturition in an unarborized state.
source: Following primary pathway outgrowth through the medial forebrain bundle (MFB), ascending 5-HT axons originating in the dorsal raphe (DRN), median raphe (MRN) and B9 groups of midbrain/pons 5-HT neurons are selectively routed along pre-existing fiber tracts and reach all forebrain targets at parturition in an unarborized state (Bang et al., 2012; Lidov and Molliver, 1982; Muzerelle et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Descending 5-HT axons enter the spinal cord via the dorsolateral and ventral funiculi.
source: Descending 5-HT axons, originating in the medullary serotonergic clusters, raphe pallidus (RPa), raphe obscurus (ROb), and raphe magnus (RMg), enter the spinal cord via the dorsolateral and ventral funiculi.
evidence: This statement is supported by the context of the paragraph and citation to Rajaofetra et al., 1989.

claim: Terminal arborization of 5-HT axons is an entirely postnatal stage of maturation.
source: After the major ascending and descending projection pathways are formed, a final, entirely postnatal, stage of 5-HT projection pathway maturation ensues during which 5-HT axons originating in different anatomically defined sub-regions flourish profuse terminal arbors in complementary and topographically organized patterns (Muzerelle et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Terminal arborization develops at least through the first four postnatal weeks.
source: Terminal arborization develops at least through the first four postnatal weeks and leaves few, if any, regions of the brain and spinal cord devoid of serotonergic input (Gagnon and Parent, 2014; Hornung, 2003; Lidov and Molliver, 1982; Maddaloni et al., 2017; Steinbusch, 1981).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lmx1b is a crucial factor in 5-HT gene regulatory networks.
source: The LIM homeodomain protein, Lmx1b, is a crucial factor in 5-HT GRNs as 5-HT neuron selective targeting of Lmx1b results in the failure to induce Tph2 expression for 5-HT synthesis and Slc6a4 expression for 5-HT reuptake (Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 5-HT neuron selective targeting of Lmx1b results in the failure to induce Tph2 expression for 5-HT synthesis.
source: The LIM homeodomain protein, Lmx1b, is a crucial factor in 5-HT GRNs as 5-HT neuron selective targeting of Lmx1b results in the failure to induce Tph2 expression for 5-HT synthesis and Slc6a4 expression for 5-HT reuptake (Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 5-HT neuron selective targeting of Lmx1b results in the failure to induce Slc6a4 expression for 5-HT reuptake.
source: The LIM homeodomain protein, Lmx1b, is a crucial factor in 5-HT GRNs as 5-HT neuron selective targeting of Lmx1b results in the failure to induce Tph2 expression for 5-HT synthesis and Slc6a4 expression for 5-HT reuptake (Zhao et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lmx1b targeting results in extremely low levels of 5-HT in the adult brain.
source: This results in extremely low levels of 5-HT in the adult brain, which is associated with high neonatal mortality and several abnormal behavioral phenotypes including hyperactivity, delayed respiratory maturation, enhanced inflammatory pain sensitivity, deficient opioid analgesia, sleep regulation, and increased contextual fear memories (Dai et al., 2008; Hodges et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2007a; Zhao et al., 2007b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Low 5-HT levels due to Lmx1b targeting are associated with high neonatal mortality.
source: This results in extremely low levels of 5-HT in the adult brain, which is associated with high neonatal mortality and several abnormal behavioral phenotypes including hyperactivity, delayed respiratory maturation, enhanced inflammatory pain sensitivity, deficient opioid analgesia, sleep regulation, and increased contextual fear memories (Dai et al., 2008; Hodges et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2007a; Zhao et al., 2007b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lmx1b is a continuously expressed, terminal selector-type factor in 5-HT neurons.
source: Lmx1b is a continuously expressed, terminal selector-type factor in 5-HT neurons (Hobert, 2008) raising the possibility that subsequent to its initial role in the induction of 5-HT synthesis and transport it may perform additional stage specific functions in the maturation of serotonergic connectivity.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In control adult mice, 82% of Tph2+ neurons in the DRN and MRN express TdTomato.
source: In control adult mice, 82% of Tph2+ neurons in the DRN and MRN express TdTomato.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Approximately 88% of TdTomato+ cells co-label with Tph2 in control mice.
source: Conversely, approximately 88% of TdTomato+ cells co-label with Tph2; the remaining TdTomato+ cells likely express Tph2, but at a level insufficient for detection with standard IHC (Deneris and Gaspar, 2018; Okaty et al., 2015) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: TdTomato+ cells were not found outside of the raphe nuclei in control mice.
source: TdTomato+ cells were not found outside of the raphe nuclei (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TdTomato+ axons in control mice colocalized with 5-HT.
source: TdTomato+ axons in control mice were widely distributed throughout the adult brain and colocalized with 5-HT (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The pattern of TdTomato+ axons in the control forebrain corresponded closely with the pattern of 5-HT axon distribution previously determined in the rat.
source: The pattern of TdTomato+ axons in the control forebrain corresponded closely with the pattern of 5-HT axon distribution previously determined in the rat with an anti-5-HT antibody (Lidov and Molliver, 1982; Steinbusch, 1981).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and comparison with current data.

claim: TdTomato+ axon distribution in control brains was highly concordant with 5-HT axon projection patterns determined in a mouse line with GFP knocked into the Tph2 coding region.
source: Similarly, TdTomato+ axon distribution in control brains was highly concordant with 5-HT axon projection patterns determined more recently using a mouse line in which GFP was knocked into the Tph2 coding region, thus validating our surrogate marking of 5-HT axons using a soluble reporter (Migliarini et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and comparison with current data.

claim: Abundant numbers of TdTomato+ cell bodies were detected in each of the raphe nuclei of Lmx1bcKO animals.
source: Abundant numbers of TdTomato+ cell bodies were detected in each of the raphe nuclei of Lmx1bcKO animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The vast majority of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not co-express Lmx1b or Tph2.
source: The vast majority of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not co-express Lmx1b or Tph2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: RT-qPCR analyses verified severe deficits of Lmx1b and Tph2 mRNAs in flow sorted YFP-labeled Pet1+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Further, RT-qPCR analyses verified severe deficits of Lmx1b and Tph2 mRNAs in flow sorted YFP-labeled Pet1+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice, confirming appropriate Lmx1b targeting (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Counts of TdTomato+ cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice indicated that equivalent numbers were present compared to controls at 3 months.
source: Counts of TdTomato+ cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice indicated that equivalent numbers were present compared to controls at 3 months and that their numbers remained stable for at least 13 months (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: TdTomato+ cell body numbers in Lmx1bcKO mice remained stable for at least 13 months.
source: Counts of TdTomato+ cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice indicated that equivalent numbers were present compared to controls at 3 months and that their numbers remained stable for at least 13 months (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cell bodies were located within the normal cytoarchitectural boundaries of the raphe nuclei with a mildly altered distribution and smaller size.
source: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cell bodies were located within the normal cytoarchitectural boundaries of the raphe nuclei with a mildly altered distribution and smaller size (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I,J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1I,J.

claim: TdTomato+ axons were present in normal density and with proper ascending trajectory within the MFB of Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Although TdTomato+ axons were present in normal density and with proper ascending trajectory within the MFB of Lmx1bcKO mice, TdTomato+ axons were nearly completely missing throughout the forebrain of Lmx1bcKO animals distal to the thalamus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: TdTomato+ axons were nearly completely missing throughout the forebrain of Lmx1bcKO animals distal to the thalamus.
source: Although TdTomato+ axons were present in normal density and with proper ascending trajectory within the MFB of Lmx1bcKO mice, TdTomato+ axons were nearly completely missing throughout the forebrain of Lmx1bcKO animals distal to the thalamus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: The vast majority of TdTomato+ axons failed to reach various distal fiber tracts including the fimbria-fornix, supracallosal stria, cingulum bundle, and olfactory tract in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Indeed, the vast majority of TdTomato+ axons failed to reach various distal fiber tracts including the fimbria-fornix, supracallosal stria, cingulum bundle, and olfactory tract (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: Few if any TdTomato+ axons were present in the olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, striatum or many regions of the hypothalamus in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Consequently, few if any TdTomato+ axons were present in the olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, striatum or many regions of the hypothalamus (Figure 1B–D; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B–D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: TdTomato+ axons were present in the thalamus of Lmx1bcKO mice, but the distribution of their terminal arbors was different from controls.
source: Although Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons were present in the thalamus, the distribution of their terminal arbors was quite different from that in controls (Figure 1B,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1B,E.

claim: Aberrant clumping of mutant TdTomato+ terminal arbors was found in several intralaminar thalamic nuclei of Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: We found aberrant clumping of mutant TdTomato+ terminal arbors in several intralaminar thalamic nuclei (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Many regions of the thalamus were completely devoid of arbors in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Many regions were completely devoid of arbors unlike the relatively homogeneously tiled distribution in the control thalamus (Figure 1E, arrowheads).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1E.

claim: The conspicuously dense 5-HT arborization that demarcates the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT) was completely absent in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: In addition, the conspicuously dense 5-HT arborization that demarcates the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT) was completely absent in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: AAV2 virus injection confirmed the absence of YFP+ axons in all distal areas where TdTomato+ axons were absent in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: In Lmx1bcKO mice, we found an absence of YFP+ axons in all of the distal areas in which TdTomato+ axons were absent.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the viral injection experiment.

claim: YFP+ axons were colocalized in all forebrain areas with TdTomato+ axons in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Moreover, YFP+ axons were colocalized in all forebrain areas with TdTomato+ axons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K,L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1K,L.

claim: In control animals, 80% of Tph2+ medullary cell bodies expressed TdTomato.
source: In control animals, 80% of Tph2+ medullary cell bodies expressed TdTomato and 92% of TdTomato+ cell bodies were co-labeled with Tph2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 92% of TdTomato+ cell bodies were co-labeled with Tph2 in control medullary neurons.
source: In control animals, 80% of Tph2+ medullary cell bodies expressed TdTomato and 92% of TdTomato+ cell bodies were co-labeled with Tph2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TdTomato+ axon patterns in control E15.5 embryos corresponded closely with the pattern of developing 5-HT-labeled axons in the ventral and lateral funiculi of the spinal cord.
source: TdTomato+ axon patterns in control E15.5 embryos corresponded closely with the pattern of developing 5-HT-labeled axons in the ventral and lateral funiculi of the spinal cord, thus indicating specific labeling of descending 5-HT axons with TdTomato (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The pattern of control TdTomato+ axon distribution throughout the embryonic and adult spinal cord corresponded to descending 5-HT axons patterns described in the rat and mouse.
source: In addition, the pattern of control TdTomato+ axon distribution throughout the embryonic and adult spinal cord corresponded to descending 5-HT axons patterns in gray and white matter described in the rat and mouse with an anti-5-HT antibody (Ballion et al., 2002; Rajaofetra et al., 1989).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature and comparison with current data.

claim: The number of TdTomato-labeled Pet1+ neurons in the medullary raphe nuclei did not differ between Lmx1bcKO and control mice at 3 months of age.
source: We confirmed that the number of TdTomato-labeled Pet1+ neurons in the medullary raphe nuclei did not differ between Lmx1bcKO and control mice at 3 months of age (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not express Tph2 in medullary neurons.
source: Further, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells did not express Tph2, confirming targeting of Lmx1b (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A severe lack of TdTomato+ axons was found in the white matter funiculi of Lmx1bcKO spinal cords.
source: We found a severe lack of TdTomato+ axons in the white matter funiculi, through which 5-HT axon projections normally extend caudally through the spinal cord (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A severe reduction of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons was found in gray matter at all levels of the spinal cord.
source: In addition, a severe reduction of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons was found in gray matter at all levels of the spinal cord (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: The normally dense innervation to the dorsal and ventral horns of control spinal cords was dramatically decreased in cervical, thoracic and lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: The normally dense innervation to the dorsal and ventral horns of control spinal cords was dramatically decreased in cervical, thoracic and lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter while at lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: At lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: At cervical levels there was a 67% deficit of TdTomato+ axons in white matter while at lumbar levels there was a 92% deficit (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a 73% deficit at cervical levels in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords.
source: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a progressive cervical to lumbar deficit, 73% and 94%, respectively in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a 94% deficit at lumbar levels in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords.
source: Quantitation of TdTomato+ axons in gray matter revealed a progressive cervical to lumbar deficit, 73% and 94%, respectively in Lmx1bcKO cords compared to control cords (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: The deficit in 5-HT axons becomes increasingly profound with increasing distance from 5-HT cell bodies in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Collectively, our results indicate that Lmx1b deficiency severely disrupts long-range 5-HT axon architecture in the forebrain and spinal cord and that the deficit becomes increasingly profound with increasing distance from 5-HT cell bodies.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: At E13.5, TdTomato+ axon outgrowth and trajectory in Lmx1bcKO mice were normal as they coursed through the MFB over the mesencephalic flexure.
source: We first investigated TdTomato+ axons at E13.5 when primary pathway formation is underway and Lmx1b conditional targeting has occurred. At this stage, TdTomato+ axon outgrowth and trajectory in Lmx1bcKO mice were normal as they coursed through the MFB over the mesencephalic flexure (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: At E16.5, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons exhibited a clear failure to extend as far rostrally as control axons.
source: At E16.5, however, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons exhibited a clear failure to extend as far rostrally as control axons, suggesting either aborted or delayed axon outgrowth along the more rostral portions of the MFB during late stage primary pathway formation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: At E18.5, the density of control TdTomato+ axons was maximal throughout the MFB.
source: At E18.5, the density of control TdTomato+ axons was maximal throughout the MFB and TdTomato+ axons were present as far rostral as the septum and diagonal band, where 5-HT axons turn dorsally to navigate through the cingulum, supracallosal stria, and fimbria-fornix (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: At E18.5, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appeared at normal density throughout the MFB.
source: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons now appeared at normal density throughout the MFB, thus supporting delayed axon outgrowth at E16.5 (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: At E18.5, most Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons failed to turn dorsally and remained stalled within the MFB.
source: However, at this stage, most Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons failed to turn dorsally and remained stalled within the MFB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: A smaller number of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did turn dorsally away from the MFB to pass through the septum and diagonal band at E18.5.
source: A smaller number of Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did turn dorsally away from the MFB to pass through the septum and diagonal band (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: Virtually all Lmx1bcKO axons failed to extend and selectively route into the cingulum and fimbria-fornix at E18.5.
source: Virtually all Lmx1bcKO axons failed to extend and selectively route into the cingulum and fimbria-fornix, thus failing to reach the cortex and hippocampus.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons did not exhibit ectopic trajectories at E18.5.
source: Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons still did not exhibit ectopic trajectories.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Conditional targeting of Lmx1b at E12.5 results in delayed primary pathway formation followed by a profound failure of ascending axons to selectively route into pre-existing fiber tracts.
source: These findings suggest that conditional targeting of Lmx1b at E12.5 results in delayed primary pathway formation followed by a profound failure of ascending axons to selectively route into pre-existing fiber tracts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: At E15.5, TdTomato+ fibers showed similar initial axon outgrowth through the caudal medulla to the upper cervical spinal cord from Lmx1bcKO and control medullary 5-HT cell bodies.
source: Analysis of descending TdTomato+ fibers at E15.5 revealed similar initial axon outgrowth through the caudal medulla to the upper cervical spinal cord from Lmx1bcKO and control medullary 5-HT cell bodies (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Although Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appropriately entered the lateral and ventral funiculi of the cervical spinal cord, greatly reduced densities were evident beginning at mid-cervical levels.
source: Although Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons appropriately entered the lateral and ventral funiculi of the cervical spinal cord, greatly reduced densities were evident beginning at mid-cervical levels (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: At lumbar levels, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons were nearly undetectable in the lateral and ventral funiculi.
source: At lumbar levels, Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ axons were nearly undetectable in the lateral and ventral funiculi (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: TdTomato+ axons were not able to extend into the funiculi, which caused a severe and progressive cervical to lumbar deficit of 5-HT innervation in the adult Lmx1bcKO spinal cord.
source: These results indicate that TdTomato+ axons were not able to extend into the funiculi, which caused a severe and progressive cervical to lumbar deficit of 5-HT innervation in the adult Lmx1bcKO spinal cord (Figures 2 and 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Subcutaneous delivery of tamoxifen into iControl pups resulted in approximately 94% of Tph2+ neurons co-labeled with TdTomato in the DRN/MRN/B9.
source: Subcutaneous delivery of tamoxifen into iControl pups resulted in approximately 94% of Tph2+ neurons co-labeled with TdTomato in the DRN/MRN/B9 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: 94% of TdTomato+ cells were co-labeled with Tph2 in tamoxifen-treated iControl pups.
source: Conversely, 94% of TdTomato+ cells were co-labeled with Tph2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: RT-qPCR analysis verified that Lmx1b mRNA was significantly reduced in Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: RT-qPCR analysis of flow sorted TdTomato+ cells verified that Lmx1b mRNA was significantly reduced in Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: Equivalent numbers of TdTomato-labeled cell bodies were generated in Lmx1bicKO versus iControl mice after injection of tamoxifen.
source: Equivalent numbers of TdTomato-labeled cell bodies were generated in Lmx1bicKO versus iControl mice after injection of tamoxifen (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Cell body size and distribution of tamoxifen treated Lmx1bicKO TdTomato+ cells were not different from that of iControl TdTomato+ cells.
source: In contrast to Lmx1bcKO TdTomato+ cells, cell body size and distribution of tamoxifen treated Lmx1bicKO TdTomato+ cells were not different from that of iControl TdTomato+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E.

claim: A dramatic deficit in TdTomato+ arbors was found throughout the hippocampus in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: We found a dramatic deficit in TdTomato+ arbors throughout the hippocampus in Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C.

claim: TdTomato+ arbors were severely reduced in all layers of the cortex in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: In addition, TdTomato+ arbors were severely reduced in all layers of the cortex with the most medial layers almost completely devoid of arbors in Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: Lmx1b is temporally required for postnatal development of 5-HT terminal axons.
source: These results clearly demonstrate that Lmx1b is temporally required for postnatal development of 5-HT terminal axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: TdTomato labeling within the supracallosal stria and cingulum was consistently less intense in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls.
source: However, we noticed that in addition to reduced 5-HT arbors in the hippocampus and cortex, TdTomato labeling within the supracallosal stria and cingulum, major routes to the hippocampus and cortex, were consistently less intense in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4C, asterisk).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4C.

claim: Major 5-HT routes (supracallosal stria and cingulum) had not yet fully formed in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: Indeed, further detailed examination revealed that these major 5-HT routes had not yet fully formed (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4E.

claim: Quantification confirmed a significant decrease in TdTomato+ axons within the cingulum and supracallosal stria tracts in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls.
source: Quantification of TdTomato+ axons within the cingulum and supracallosal stria tracts confirmed a significant decrease in P1 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice compared to controls (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4F.

claim: Long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period.
source: These results indicate that i, long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period and ii, Lmx1b is required at this stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Lmx1b is required at the P1 stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
source: These results indicate that i, long-range 5-HT axon routing is continuing to develop in the early neonatal period and ii, Lmx1b is required at this stage for completion of 5-HT axon selective routing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The density of TdTomato-labeled fibers in the supracallosal stria was similar in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.
source: Importantly, in contrast to findings obtained in P1 targeted mice, we found that the density of TdTomato-labeled fibers in the supracallosal stria was now similar in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TdTomato-labeled fibers in the cingulum were comparable in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.
source: Furthermore, TdTomato-labeled fibers in the cingulum, one of the longest of 5-HT forebrain tracts, was now comparable in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B.

claim: Quantification confirmed no significant difference in the cingulum and supracallosal stria between P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice.
source: Quantification of the cingulum and supracallosal stria confirmed no significant difference between P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO and iControl mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 5-HT axon routing was complete in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: These findings indicate that 5-HT axon routing was complete in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: TdTomato+ arbors were significantly decreased throughout the hippocampus in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: Despite fully developed 5-HT selective pathway routes in the forebrain, TdTomato+ arbors were significantly decreased throughout the hippocampus (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A majority of remaining arbors detected within the hippocampus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice were found in the molecular layer (SLM).
source: A majority of remaining arbors detected within the hippocampus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice were found in the molecular layer (SLM), which are the first 5-HT arbors to appear in the hippocampus during rat development (Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: TdTomato+ arbors were severely decreased in all cortical layers of the P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO brain.
source: TdTomato+ arbors were also severely decreased in all cortical layers of the P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO brain including in layer I and VI where axons of passage also exist (Figure 5D) (Lidov and Molliver, 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Quantification confirmed a significant decrease of TdTomato+ axon arbors in the cortex of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO compared to iControls.
source: Quantification of the cortex confirmed a significant decrease of TdTomato+ axon arbors in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO compared to iControls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Many 5-HT terminal arbors have already been generated in the forebrain at P3.
source: It is important to note that many 5-HT terminal arbors have already been generated in the forebrain at P3 (Lidov and Molliver, 1982; Maddaloni et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lmx1b targeting at P3 results in the failure of new arbors to form while leaving previously generated arbors intact.
source: Thus, Lmx1b targeting at P3 results in the failure of new arbors to form while leaving previously generated arbors intact.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Arborization deficits were found within the thalamus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: Interestingly, arborization deficits were also found within the thalamus of P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The normally dense arborization within the PVT was absent in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: Similar to what we observed in Lmx1bcKO mice, the normally dense arborization within the PVT was absent in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice, rendering the PVT indiscernible (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5E.

claim: Lmx1b switches to control terminal arborization of forebrain 5-HT axons at a successive stage.
source: Together, these results reveal a successive stage of continuous Lmx1b function during which it switches to control terminal arborization of forebrain 5-HT axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The numbers of TdTomato+ cells in each raphe nuclei did not differ in Tph2cKO and control mice.
source: The numbers of TdTomato+ cells in each raphe nuclei did not differ in Tph2cKO and control mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: A 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons was found in Tph2cKO mice in the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei.
source: In the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei, we found a 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Tph2cKO compared to the 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B,C.

claim: A 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons was found in Lmx1bcKO mice in the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei.
source: In the DRN/MRN/B9 nuclei, we found a 74% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Tph2cKO compared to the 79% reduction of Tph2+ neurons in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6B,C.

claim: Loss of 5-HT itself was confirmed in Tph2cKO mice.
source: Additionally, we confirmed loss of 5-HT itself in Tph2cKO mice (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6D.

claim: No differences in Tph2cKO versus control TdTomato-labeled arbor patterns were found anywhere in the forebrain including the hippocampus, cortex, and the PVT.
source: We analyzed TdTomato+ terminal arbors throughout the forebrain in adult Tph2cKO mice. We did not find differences in Tph2cKO versus control TdTomato-labeled arbor patterns anywhere in the forebrain including the hippocampus, cortex, and the PVT (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6E.

claim: Analysis of the spinal cord from cervical to lumbar levels revealed no differences in axon densities in Tph2cKO compared to control mice.
source: Further, despite loss of Tph2 in medullary neurons of Tph2cKO mice (Figure 6F), analysis of the spinal cord from cervical to lumbar levels revealed no differences in axon densities compared to control mice (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6F,G.

claim: The loss of Tph2 and reduced levels of 5-HT in Lmx1bcKO or Lmx1bicKO mice did not contribute to either the routing or arborization defects.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the loss of Tph2 and thus reduced levels of 5-HT in Lmx1bcKO or Lmx1bicKO mice did not contribute to either the routing or arborization defects.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Known Lmx1b target genes (Tph2, Slc18a2, Slc6a4, SCG II, Ctr) were significantly decreased in E17.5 rostral and caudal Lmx1bcKO datasets.
source: Differential expression analysis revealed that the known Lmx1b target genes, Tph2, Slc18a2, Slc6a4, SCG II, Ctr, were significantly decreased in our E17.5 rostral and caudal Lmx1bcKO datasets.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Other 5-HT pathway genes (Ddc, Slc22a3, Htr1a, Gch1, Gchfr) were significantly decreased in both rostral and caudal Lmx1bcKO sorted 5-HT neurons.
source: Moreover, we found significantly decreased expression of other 5-HT pathway genes, Ddc, Slc22a3, Htr1a, Gch1, Gchfr, in both rostral and caudal Lmx1bcKO sorted 5-HT neurons that were previously unknown Lmx1b targets (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7B,C based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: In rostral Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 784 genes were significantly decreased.
source: In rostral Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 784 genes were significantly decreased, while 118 genes showed significantly increased expression (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7F,G based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: In rostral Lmx1bcKO neurons, 118 genes showed significantly increased expression.
source: In rostral Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 784 genes were significantly decreased, while 118 genes showed significantly increased expression (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7F,G based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: In caudal Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 1529 genes were significantly decreased.
source: In caudal Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 1529 genes were significantly decreased and 772 were significantly increased (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7F,G based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: In caudal Lmx1bcKO neurons, 772 genes were significantly increased.
source: In caudal Lmx1bcKO neurons, expression of 1529 genes were significantly decreased and 772 were significantly increased (Figure 7F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7F,G based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Many genes were commonly regulated by Lmx1b in rostral and caudal 5-HT neurons, but many more were uniquely regulated.
source: Although there were many genes commonly regulated by Lmx1b, many more were uniquely regulated by Lmx1b in rostral versus caudal 5-HT neurons (Figure 7F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7F–H based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Over-representation analysis of Gene Ontology (GO) terms revealed strong enrichment for genes involved in axon development and morphogenesis.
source: Over-representation analysis of Gene Ontology (GO) terms from rostral and caudal Lmx1b-regulated 5-HT neuron genes revealed a pattern of strong enrichment for genes involved in axon development and morphogenesis (Figure 7I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7I based on GO analysis.

claim: The top enriched GO term was axon development, representing over 150 genes with a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value of 0.
source: In fact, the top enriched GO term, axon development, represents over 150 genes with a Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjusted p-value of 0.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on GO analysis.

claim: 422 genes regulated by Lmx1b in rostral and/or caudal 5-HT neurons have known roles in axon development or function.
source: Grouping the genes from all of these axon-related categories together produced a dataset of 422 genes regulated by Lmx1b in rostral and/or caudal 5-HT neurons that have known roles in axon development or function (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on GO analysis.

claim: Sixty-six axon-related downstream genes were significantly altered in both the ascending and descending 5-HT subsystems.
source: Sixty-six of these downstream genes were significantly altered in both the ascending and descending 5-HT subsystems; 71 genes were uniquely altered in the ascending subsystem while 285 were uniquely altered in the descending subsystem.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 71 axon-related genes were uniquely altered in the ascending subsystem.
source: Sixty-six of these downstream genes were significantly altered in both the ascending and descending 5-HT subsystems; 71 genes were uniquely altered in the ascending subsystem while 285 were uniquely altered in the descending subsystem.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 285 axon-related genes were uniquely altered in the descending subsystem.
source: Sixty-six of these downstream genes were significantly altered in both the ascending and descending 5-HT subsystems; 71 genes were uniquely altered in the ascending subsystem while 285 were uniquely altered in the descending subsystem.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Lmx1b coordinates distinct axonal regulatory programs and transcriptomes to build the two divergent axonal subsystems.
source: This analysis suggests that Lmx1b coordinates distinct axonal regulatory programs and transcriptomes to build the two divergent axonal subsystems.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Examination of rostral and caudal RNA-seq datasets revealed significantly decreased expression of most previously implicated 5-HT axon genes.
source: Examination of our rostral and caudal RNA-seq datasets revealed significantly decreased expression of most but not all of these genes (Figure 7J,K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7J,K based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Decreased Pet1 expression was the most consistent and persistent change among the regulatory factors in the rostral and caudal 5-HT GRNs after conditional targeting of Lmx1b.
source: Decreased Pet1 expression was the most consistent and persistent change among the regulatory factors in the rostral and caudal 5-HT GRNs after conditional targeting of Lmx1b, which raised the possibility that an Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade acts in the formation of 5-HT axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: TdTomato+ axon patterns from cervical to lumbar levels of the spinal cord were similar in Pet1cKO and control mice.
source: We first examined TdTomato+ axon patterns in adult Pet1cKO versus control spinal cords. We confirmed Pet1 transcript loss in medullary 5-HT neurons by in situ hybridization (ISH) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A). TdTomato+ axon patterns from cervical to lumbar levels of the spinal cord were similar in Pet1cKO and control mice (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8A.

claim: Quantitation of total TdTomato+ axons in gray and white matter revealed no significant difference between Pet1cKO and control mice.
source: Quantitation of total TdTomato+ axons in gray and white matter revealed no significant difference between Pet1cKO and control mice (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8B.

claim: Pet1 is not required for the formation of descending 5-HT axon pathways.
source: These findings indicate that Pet1, and consequently the hypothetical Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade, is not required for the formation of descending 5-HT axon pathways (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Few if any TdTomato+ axons were present in the olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, striatum and many regions of the hypothalamus in Pet1cKO forebrains.
source: We next investigated the Pet1cKO forebrain and found in striking contrast to the spinal cord that few if any TdTomato+ axons were present in the olfactory bulb, cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, striatum and many regions of the hypothalamus in Pet1cKO forebrains (Figure 8C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8C–E.

claim: The pattern of TdTomato+ axons in the thalamus of Pet1cKO mice was severely disrupted with notable patches of clumped fibers and other areas with few, if any, fibers.
source: Furthermore, the pattern of TdTomato+ axons in the thalamus of Pet1cKO mice was severely disrupted with notable patches of clumped fibers and other areas with few, if any, fibers (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TdTomato+ axons were present in normal density and with proper ascending trajectory within the MFB of Pet1cKO mice.
source: Similar to Lmx1bcKO mice, TdTomato+ axons were present in normal density and with proper ascending trajectory within the MFB of Pet1cKO mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Pet1 is required for forebrain 5-HT pathway formation.
source: These findings clearly demonstrate a requirement for Pet1 in forebrain 5-HT pathway formation and thus distinct transcription factor requirements in the generation of ascending and descending 5-HT axon projection pathways.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: There are distinct transcription factor requirements in the generation of ascending and descending 5-HT axon projection pathways.
source: These findings clearly demonstrate a requirement for Pet1 in forebrain 5-HT pathway formation and thus distinct transcription factor requirements in the generation of ascending and descending 5-HT axon projection pathways.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The Pet1cKO thalamus lacked TdTomato+ axons in lateral regions.
source: Although Pet1 conditional targeting largely phenocopies the forebrain 5-HT axon defects found in Lmx1bcKO mice, we noticed distinctly different patterns of TdTomato+ arbors in the Pet1cKO vs. Lmx1bcKO thalamus (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B). The Pet1cKO thalamus lacked TdTomato+ axons in lateral regions while in other thalamic regions we found abnormal clumping of Pet1cKO TdTomato+ axons (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Abnormal clumping of Pet1cKO TdTomato+ axons was found in some thalamic regions.
source: The Pet1cKO thalamus lacked TdTomato+ axons in lateral regions while in other thalamic regions we found abnormal clumping of Pet1cKO TdTomato+ axons (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In contrast to the failure of Lmx1bcKO axons to demarcate the PVT, Pet1cKO TdTomato+ axons were properly patterned in this region.
source: Further, in contrast to the failure of Lmx1bcKO axons to demarcate the PVT, Pet1cKO TdTomato+ axons were properly patterned in this region (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lmx1b may act independently of Pet1 in the PVT.
source: This suggests Lmx1b may act independently of Pet1 in this specific highly discrete target field.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data.

claim: Early Pet1 deficiency did not result in reduced cell body size.
source: Interestingly, early Pet1 deficiency did not result in reduced cell body size thus demonstrating that reduced cell body size did not contribute to the axon defects in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Reduced cell body size did not contribute to the axon defects in Lmx1bcKO mice.
source: Interestingly, early Pet1 deficiency did not result in reduced cell body size thus demonstrating that reduced cell body size did not contribute to the axon defects in Lmx1bcKO mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data.

claim: Lmx1b→Pet1 is the main regulatory program but additional minor Lmx1b- or Pet1-orchestrated regulatory pathways operate in building ascending 5-HT axonal architectures.
source: The robust similarities and yet distinct differences in TdTomato+ axon patterns in Pet1cKO compared to Lmx1bcKO forebrain support a model in which Lmx1b→Pet1 is the main regulatory program but that additional minor Lmx1b- or Pet1-orchestrated regulatory pathways operate in building ascending 5-HT axonal architectures (Figure 8—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Analysis of DKO spinal cords revealed deficits in TdTomato+ axons patterns to similar levels as Lmx1bcKO spinal cord.
source: Analysis of DKO spinal cords revealed deficits in TdTomato+ axons patterns to similar levels as Lmx1bcKO spinal cord, further confirming Pet1 does not play a role in descending 5-HT axon development (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A more extreme deficit in TdTomato+ axons was not found in DKO mice compared to Lmx1bcKO mice in the forebrain.
source: In the forebrain, we did not find a more extreme deficit in TdTomato+ axons in DKO mice compared to Lmx1bcKO mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The DKO thalamus mirrored the Lmx1bcKO thalamus in the specific clumping of arbors and inability to properly pattern arbors in the PVT.
source: The DKO thalamus mirrored the Lmx1bcKO thalamus in the specific clumping of arbors and inability to properly pattern arbors in the PVT (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Comparable initial 5-HT primary axon outgrowth was found in Pet1-/- and control 5-HT neuron cell bodies at E13.5.
source: To investigate whether the initial 1–2 days of Pet1 expression, not targeted by Pet1-Cre in Pet1cKO mice is required for primary ascending pathway formation, we analyzed Pet1-/-;Pet1-YFP mice in which the Pet1-YFP transgene labels control and mutant Pet1+ cell bodies and their axons with YFP (Hawthorne et al., 2010). We found comparable initial 5-HT primary axon outgrowth in Pet1-/- and control 5-HT neuron cell bodies at E13.5 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 8—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Lmx1b continues to control Pet1 postnatally as Pet1 transcript levels were decreased in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice.
source: We found that Lmx1b continues to control Pet1 postnatally as Pet1 transcript levels were decreased in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 9A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9A,B.

claim: 82 regulated genes were present in both rostral Lmx1b and Pet1 datasets.
source: Comparing rostral Lmx1b and Pet1 regulated genes, we found 82 regulated genes present in both datasets (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9C based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 15 co-regulated genes were found by intersecting rostral Lmx1b and Pet1 regulated genes with the set of Lmx1b-regulated axon-related genes.
source: By intersecting rostral Lmx1b and Pet1 regulated genes with the set of Lmx1b-regulated axon-related genes (Supplementary file 1), we found 15 co-regulated genes (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9C based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Pcdhac2 is one of the coregulated genes by Lmx1b and Pet1.
source: Interestingly, one of these coregulated genes is Pcdhac2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Pcdhac2 has a key intrinsic role in the formation and patterning 5-HT axon arbors.
source: Extensive studies of Pcdhac2 have demonstrated its key intrinsic role in the formation and patterning 5-HT axon arbors (Chen et al., 2017; Katori et al., 2009; Katori et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pcdhac2 deficient mice exhibit a lack of forebrain 5-HT arbors and severe clumping of remaining arbors.
source: In particular, Pcdhac2 deficient mice exhibit a lack of forebrain 5-HT arbors and severe clumping of remaining arbors, thus raising a functional link to Lmx1b and Pet1.
evidence: This statement is supported by the context and previous citations.

claim: Pcdhac2 was significantly regulated by Lmx1b and Pet1 at E17.5.
source: By testing the only unique exon for Pcdhac2, we found that Pcdhac2 was significantly regulated by Lmx1b and Pet1 at E17.5 (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9D based on differential exon expression analysis.

claim: Pcdhac2 expression was not significantly regulated by Pet1 at earlier stages.
source: In contrast, Pcdhac2 expression was not significantly regulated by Pet1 at earlier stages (Wyler et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Time-series RNA-seq analyses showed a significant and dramatic upregulation of Pcdhac2 only at the onset of the arborization stage.
source: Furthermore, our time-series RNA-seq analyses (Wyler et al., 2016) showed a significant and dramatic upregulation of Pcdhac2 only at the onset of the arborization stage (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9E based on time-series RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Pcdhac2 expression is precisely controlled at the stage in which it is required for morphological maturation of 5-HT neurons.
source: Thus, Pcdhac2 expression is precisely controlled at the stage in which it is required for morphological maturation of 5-HT neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Lmx1b was required to control the postnatal upregulation of Pcdhac2.
source: To determine whether Lmx1b was required to control the postnatal upregulation of Pcdhac2, we treated Lmx1bicKO mice with tamoxifen at postnatal day three and analyzed Pcdhac2 expression by ISH at P14, when arborization is profusely developing. Indeed, we found substantially reduced expression of Pcdhac2 in P3 Lmx1bicKO mice (Figure 9F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9F.

claim: Pet1 was required for the dramatic postnatal upregulation of Pcdhac2 expression.
source: Interestingly, we found that Pet1 was also required for the dramatic postnatal upregulation of Pcdhac2 expression (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9G.

claim: The Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade acts during the arborization stage to temporally control Pcdhac2 upregulation.
source: These findings show that the Lmx1b→Pet1 regulatory cascade acts during the arborization stage to temporally control Pcdhac2 upregulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: Two significant mycPet1 ChIP-seq peaks were identified throughout the entire 250 kb Pcdha locus.
source: To determine if Pcdhac2 is a direct target of Lmx1b→Pet1, we analyzed our previously published ChIP-seq datasets (Wyler et al., 2016) for mycPet1 binding sites within the Pcdhac2 locus. Notably, we identified only two significant mycPet1 ChIP-seq peaks throughout the entire 250 kb Pcdha locus (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9H based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: One mycPet1 peak was located at the 5' end of the unique Pcdhac2 first exon.
source: One peak was located at the 5' end of the unique Pcdhac2 first exon.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: The second mycPet1 peak was located precisely within the third-intronic DNase I hypersensitivity site, HS7.
source: The second peak was located precisely within the third-intronic DNase I hypersensitivity site, HS7, which marks a well characterized transcriptional enhancer known to regulate midbrain expression of the Pcdha gene isoform (Kehayova et al., 2011; Ribich et al., 2006) (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9H based on ChIP-seq analysis and citations to previous literature.

claim: The mycPet1 peak at the TSS of Pcdhac2 does not contain a match to the known Pet1 binding motif.
source: Although the mycPet1 peak at the TSS of Pcdhac2 does not contain a match to the known Pet1 binding motif, the second peak within HS7 does contain a significant match to the Pet1 motif (Wei et al., 2010) (Figure 9I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9I based on motif analysis.

claim: The second mycPet1 peak within HS7 contains a significant match to the Pet1 motif.
source: Although the mycPet1 peak at the TSS of Pcdhac2 does not contain a match to the known Pet1 binding motif, the second peak within HS7 does contain a significant match to the Pet1 motif (Wei et al., 2010) (Figure 9I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9I based on motif analysis.

claim: Analyses performed at P49 revealed a severe deficit of 5-HT arbors in the hippocampus and cortex of P3 targeted Pet1icKO mice.
source: To determine whether Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade acts postnatally to control terminal arborization we analyzed the forebrains of P3 targeted Pet1icKO mice. Analyses performed at P49 revealed a severe deficit of 5-HT arbors in the hippocampus and cortex of P3 targeted Pet1icKO mice, comparable to the deficit found in P3 targeted Lmx1bicKO mice (Figures 5C, 5D; Figures 9J, 9K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figures 9J, 9K.

claim: A notable deficit in the 5-HT arbors was found throughout the striatum in P5 targeted Pet1icKO mice.
source: Interestingly, we found a notable deficit in the 5-HT arbors throughout the striatum (Figure 9L; Figure 9—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 9L and Figure 9—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade operates continually over an extended postnatal period to control stage-specific gene expression and to generate both early and late 5-HT terminal arbors patterns in different forebrain regions.
source: Together, our findings demonstrate that the Lmx1b→Pet1 cascade operates continually over an extended postnatal period to control stage-specific gene expression and to generate both early and late 5-HT terminal arbors patterns in different forebrain regions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: A single continuously expressed transcription factor, Lmx1b, functions at successive stages to orchestrate the progressive development of long-range axon architectures enabling expansive neuromodulation.
source: Our findings identify a temporal regulatory mechanism in which a single continuously expressed transcription factor functions at successive stages to orchestrate the progressive development of long-range axon architectures enabling expansive neuromodulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a main conclusion of the study.
